events.title: Live Aid Exhibition
events.description:
Through a series of striking displays, the exhibition brings audiences on a visual journey of the Live Aid concerts, capturing the behind-the-scenes preparations, atmosphere and iconic performances by bands and artists on both sides of the Atlantic as the day unfolded.

From Status Quo, U2 and David Bowie in London, to Black Sabbath and Run DMC in Philadelphia Live Aid at the National Library of Ireland immerses visitors in the scale and spirit of this iconic event from the intimacy of the National Photographic Archive.

This free exhibition opens to the public daily (10.00am – 4.00pm)

events.title: James Joyce Walking Tour
events.description:
A fun and exciting walking tour of James Joyce's Dublin offered by the James Joyce Centre.

Though Joyce lived most of his life outside of Ireland, Dublin would provide the backdrop for virtually all of his work. On a stroll around the inner city, our guide will explain the real-life inspiration behind some of Joyce’s most celebrated writing, demonstrating just how central the streetscape of the ‘Hibernian metropolis’ was to the author’s life and art. The tour visits such stops as Belvedere College, the Gresham Hotel, the James Joyce Statue, Davy Byrnes, and the National Library.

This is an excellent and fun introduction to Joyce in a bustling part of the city.

Every Thur, Fri & Sat at 11am. Admission to the James Joyce Centre is included.

events.title: Artist-Initiated Projects 2026
events.description:
Between January–December 2026 we will present 8 x 3-week exhibitions of new work by:

Paddy Critchley, Fiona Marron, Finn Nichol, Emma Brennan and Thomas Wells, Ciara Rodgers, Struàn Bell, Christopher Mahon, neonatus.exe

Artist-Initiated Projects at Pallas Projects/Studios is an open-submission, annual gallery programme of 8 x 3-week exhibitions taking place between January and December 2026. This unique programme of funded, artist-initiated projects selected via open call is highly accessible to artists, with a focus on early career, emerging artists and recent graduates. Projects are supplemented with artists' talks, texts, workshops or performances, and gallery visits by colleges and local schools.

events.title: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU
events.description:
Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size.

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.

events.title: Dún Laoghaire Walking Tours, The Dublin Riviera
events.description:
The Dublin Riviera is a guided walk back in time to a golden era where local Dún Laoghaire residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant, glamorous “Dublin Riviera”.

Highlights:

Waterfront Yacht Clubs and the Royal Visits

The Pavilion and Town Hall

Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens

Haddington House Hotel

Former Seafront hotels on Victoria and Marine Terrace

Dún Laoghaire Baths (finish)

events.title: Rembrandt to Matisse – A Celebration of European Works on Paper
events.description:
Drawings, prints, watercolours and photographs by a range of European artists from the fifteenth century to the present day are included. The exhibition explores the diverse subjects and styles that have shaped European art through the centuries. Reflecting shifts in taste and technique over the centuries, the exhibition showcases the strength of the Gallery’s collection across the various schools.

Curator: Niamh MacNally, Curator of the Prints and Drawings Study Room at the National Gallery of Ireland.

events.title: Technologies of Peace: Art and Transition in Contemporary Europe (1989–2026)
events.description:
In post-conflict countries, the journey towards lasting peace involves a multifaceted approach that extends beyond political, economic, and security measures. Artistic practice and cultural experience play a pivotal role in healing societies, fostering reconciliation, and building a shared sense of identity and community.

IMMA is open to the general public 6 days a week. The museum is closed on Mondays, except Bank Holidays. See full opening hours below.

events.title: 'Thinning the Veil': Art Exhibition
events.description:
Six contemporary Fingal artists come together at Malahide Castle this autumn in an exhibition exploring memory, history, heritage and the changing role of monuments in contemporary Ireland. Curated by Eamonn Maxwell, the exhibition features sculptures, installations, sound works and graphic pieces throughout the castle.

From 22 September, the programme continues with free special events including a Curator’s Tour & Artist Q&A with Eamonn Maxwell and Deborah Hewson, artist talks and exhibition tours with Ann Ensor, Laura Skehan, Michelle Hall and Susan Buttner, a live performance by Tadhg Kinsella, and a closing night exhibition tour with Cathal Dowd Smith. Advance booking is required for events.

events.title: Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design
events.description:
Our current exhibition at the National Print Museum, Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design, uses flight as a central thread to explore how design and print helped promote Irish modernisation and position Ireland internationally. With the arrival of a number of Dutch graphic designers to Ireland in the 1950s to work on advertising for Aer Lingus, depictions of Ireland and Irishness were forever changed, as was Ireland’s relationship to Continental Europe and the US. Their design work was recognised internationally and had a huge impact on Irish design and economic development.

Free admission.

events.title: EPIC x Jeanie Combo
events.description:
Take a journey back in time, get an insight into life on board a Famine ship and hear the stories of the people who made the arduous voyage.

Then head into EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum to discover what happened to those who left, and the huge global impact they managed to have all over the world.

Your experience begins at the Jeanie, and you’re free to explore EPIC at your own pace afterwards. The Jeanie is located two minutes from EPIC.

Tours occur between 10am and 3.30pm every 30 minutes - a guided Jeanie tour takes 50 minutes while visitors should leave themselves 90 minutes to explore EPIC.

events.title: Dublin by Dusk A Fair Exchange Writing Workshop
events.description:
'A Fair Exchange' takes place in a series of locations in Collins Barracks, inviting new and exciting engagements with different exhibition spaces, themes, and collections. Facilitated by poet Hazel Hogan, you are invited to engage with the workshop in the following ways:

Read a participant’s story and take a moment to reflect.

Write your own response, inspired by a story, the space, or a historic object. Write, draw, sign, or remain anonymous.

Exchange your contribution by returning it to the vessel, helping grow a collective artwork of shared reflections.

Free drop-in workshop. All materials provided. No booking required. Wheelchair accessible.

events.venue: National Museum of Ireland, Collins Barracks

events.description:

events.title: Voices of Peace Visual Art Exhibition reflecting on Peace, Equality and Human Rights
events.description:
Thursday 1 October 2026 – Sunday 29 November 2026; Wed-Fri 1-6pm, Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 12-6pm

Smashing Times Visual Art Gallery, 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin A96V9P1

Free admission.

A multidisciplinary exhibition reflecting on peace, equality and human rights through contemporary visual and creative expression. Featuring work by writer Féilim James and visual artists Jessica Rodrigues, Gillian Lambe, Viktoriia Yevsiukova, Hina Khan, Aman Walayat and Mary Moynihan, the exhibition explore peace and human rights, sparking dialogue and new visions for the future. Supported by the dlr County Council Universal Grant Scheme and the Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council Arts Office.

events.title: Hidden Histories Audio Tour Temple Bar
events.description:

Join the voices of the past as they lift the lid on the city’s most colourful district, uncovering Vikings, revolutionaries, rascals and adventurers. See the streets anew!

Tour Running Time - 39 minutes

Writer and Director: Peter Dunne, Sound Designer: Ciarán Gallagher

events.title: Roe & Co Irish Coffee Experience
events.description:
Guided by our expert hosts, enjoy a tasting of three distinctive Irish Coffee serves before crafting your own using Roe & Co Signature Blend whiskey. Along the way, uncover the history of whiskey, coffee and Irish hospitality, while learning the techniques behind the perfect Irish Coffee. Blending storytelling, hands-on cocktail making and exceptional whiskey, this experience offers a fresh take on an Irish classic and celebrates the creativity at the heart of Roe & Co.

Perfect for whiskey lovers, cocktail enthusiasts and curious travellers alike.

events.title: Evening Tours of Windmill Lane Recording Studio
events.description:
This late evening tour of Windmill Lane Recording Studios takes you behind the scenes of one of the world's most iconic music venues, where U2, The Rolling Stones, Ed Sheeran and countless other legends have recorded. Walk through the same rooms, learn how tracks are built, and even mix your own session with the virtual band. With the city quiet and the studio lights low, it's an atmospheric way to spend a winter evening in Dublin.

See Windmill Lane website for available dates.

events.title: Hilma af Klint: Artist and Visionary
events.description:
Af Klint’s art was profoundly informed by spirituality and her explorations of Rosicrucianism, Theosophy, and Anthroposophy. Like many artists of her time, she sought to make sense of and articulate the modern world.

Hilma af Klint’s spiritual paintings were seldom shown beyond her close circle. Her work remained in storage until the 1980s, largely unknown outside Sweden. This show explores the time and place that shaped her unique artistic vision.

Organised in collaboration with The Hilma af Klint Foundation.

Presented by Key Capital at 25.

Funded as part of the Culture Programme for Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union 2026.

events.title: Dublin Winter Lights Tour
events.description:
Experience the magic of Dublin during the festive season on our Winter Lights City Tour!

Sit back, relax and enjoy a journey through Dublin’s beautifully illuminated streets and landmarks as the city comes alive with festive lights and decorations.

Take in the atmosphere, admire the sparkling lights and enjoy Dublin from a different perspective as you discover the city after dark. Whether you’re visiting Dublin for the first time or seeing it with fresh eyes, the Winter Lights City Tour is a wonderful way to experience the festive charm of the capital.

Tours start at 6.00pm & 7.30pm.

events.title: Winter Solstice Tour - Experience Glasnevin
events.description:
As part of Winter in Dublin, Experience Glasnevin welcomes the public to Glasnevin Cemetery for a 60 minute Winter Solstice Tour every Friday, Saturday and Sunday between 1 Nov and 22 Dec at 12 noon. On this tour, one of our expert guides will bring you through the cemetery, exploring 200 years of Irish history through the people buried and cremated in the cemetery.

Under the Winter sky, our guides will tell the stories of remarkable figures that shaped Irish history, as well as interesting people lost to the ether of time. They will also discuss aspects of death, mourning and funerals in Irish history captured in the archive of Glasnevin Cemetery.

events.title: Festive Afternoon Tea at the Old Music Shop
events.description:
Enjoy a carefully prepared selection of delicate sandwiches, freshly baked handmade scones served with cream and jam, and an assortment of miniature desserts capturing the festive spirit, including mini mince pies, rich fruitcake, petit fours, chocolate éclairs and mousse. Complement your treats with premium organic tea, creamy hot chocolate, or a glass of bubbly for an added touch of celebration.

Whether you’re meeting friends, marking a special occasion, or simply taking a moment for yourself during the busy holiday season, our Festive Afternoon Tea offers a cosy retreat in the heart of Dublin.

Bookings available from November.

events.title: Dublin from Above
events.description:

Whether you’re planning a city break or looking to experience Dublin from a different perspective, this partnership offers the perfect combination of comfort, delicious dining and an iconic Croke Park experience.

events.title: Exhibition: Eltiqa: How to Work Together
events.description: For over twenty years, Eltiqa members have developed artistic practices together – including the setting up of a dedicated exhibition and workshop space in Gaza City, and supporting younger generations of artists through workshops, exhibitions and by offering a space to meet and dialogue. Eltiqa artists include Mohamed Abusal, Abdel Raouf Al-Ajouri, Mohammed Al-Hawajri, Raed Issa, Dina Matar and Sohail Salem.

events.venue: IMMA. Irish Museum of Modern Art

events.title: The Storytelling Trail: A Winter Journey Through Dublin
events.description:
Step into the magic of winter with The Storytelling Trail, a festive Dublin experience blending Irish folklore, seasonal traditions and warming flavours. Explore historic streets with a storyteller-guide who brings ancient legends to life, including the mysterious Cailleach, Ireland’s legendary winter goddess.

Discover Irish Christmas customs, rural traditions, festive superstitions and stories passed down through generations. Finish with a special Irish coffee-making experience, learning the story behind this iconic drink.

Blending mythology, history and flavour, The Storytelling Trail offers an immersive way to experience winter in Dublin.

events.title: The Pride Tour – Queer Irish, Global Impact
events.description:
LGBTQ+ equality in Ireland only came relatively recently. Homosexuality was only decriminalised in 1993, with marriage equality following in 2015. However, LGBTQ+ people have always been part of Ireland’s story, and for many, emigration offered the chance to live more openly.

Our Pride Tour explores some of these stories, looking at the lives of LGBTQ+ Irish emigrants, activists, artists and other figures who challenged attitudes at home and made their mark around the world.

Based in Dublin's Docklands, EPIC tells the true story of the Irish, and acts as the base for the Irish Family History Centre. It also sits across from the Jeanie Johnston Famine Ship, just 2 minutes away.

events.title: Enamel a Christmas Decoration Workshop: Dublin Stories
events.description:
Come and sip on a glass of prosecco while creating your very own beautiful, handmade enamelled Christmas decoration at our Winter in Dublin Workshop.

Inspired by the magic and character of Dublin, we’ve created a selection of charming designs for you to choose from. You’ll enamel your chosen copper design yourself, experimenting with a variety of colours and shapes to create something completely unique.

Add an extra touch of personality with a little initialled silver disc, personalised just for you and attached to your decoration.

To finish, choose your favourite festive ribbon, box up your creation and take it home with you. Ready to hang on your tree, keep as a special Christmas memento, or give as a thoughtful handmade gift.

events.title: Sip & Sleigh - A Christmas Cocktail Experience
events.description:
Shake, stir and sip your way into Christmas with Sip & Sleigh, our festive cocktail experience at Pearse Lyons Distillery.

Settle into Pearse’s Place, our very own private pub, where you’ll learn the art of mixology and create three festive cocktails using our Irish spirits.

Full of festive flavour and Christmas cheer, it’s the perfect way to enjoy winter in Dublin with friends, family or colleagues.

Come for the cocktails, stay for the Christmas spirit. 🎄🍸

events.title: Tinsel & Tonic - Christmas Gin School
events.description:
Choose from our selection of botanicals before taking to your mini copper still to distil your very own gin from start to finish. Enjoy festive bites and serves featuring our Ha’Penny and Míl Irish Gins.

With festive music playing and plenty of seasonal spirit, it’s the perfect way to enjoy Winter in Dublin with friends, family or colleagues.

Once your gin is ready, we’ll check the strength before you bottle, label and personalise your creation to take home.

Join us *Saturday's at 1pm or 4:45pm* for a festive experience with a difference – and leave with a 70cl bottle of your very own gin to enjoy over Christmas.

events.title: Love and Other Promises
events.description: LOVE AND OTHER PROMISES explores the complicated relationship between Rachel and Fiona, two women navigating co-parenting after an acrimonious breakup. When they find themselves spending time together again, old feelings and unresolved wounds begin to surface. As they grapple with betrayal, love, grief and the possibility of reconciliation, they must confront whether some relationships can ever be repaired – or whether letting go is sometimes the hardest act of love.

events.title: Rebels and Revolutionaries | Women’s History Tour
events.description:
The Rebels and Revolutionaries Women’s History Tour focuses on the ones who broke out of societal shackles to make an impact around the world. Today, we are thankfully very familiar with some of these women. The likes of Mary Robinson, Ireland’s first female president, and Countess Markievicz, an instrumental figure in the 1916 Easter Rising, are well known. But many others have been largely lost to history, despite their impressive achievements.

This tour draws attention to those left out of the history books, exploring how women’s stories have been hidden for many years and how, in modern times, historians have been revisiting, rediscovering and revealing these crucial pieces of the puzzle.

events.title: Wonderlights at Malahide Castle & Gardens
events.description:
Step onto the magic of Wonderlights, Ireland’s largest and most mesmerising winter light show experience. Welcoming over 650,000 guests to date, this award-winning spectacle transforms host venues into dazzling landscapes featuring over 3 million twinkling lights, immersive projections, and specially composed soundscapes.

Each year introduces innovative themes that blend light, colour, nature and stories into an unforgettable evening. The trail is fully accessible and suitable for all ages—ideal for family outings, date nights, or catch-ups with friends. Complete your visit at the Alpine-style food village with delicious treats, hot chocolate, and mulled wine.

events.title: Epic & Wild Lights Combo
events.description:
Start your adventure at EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, where interactive galleries, immersive exhibits and fascinating stories bring Ireland’s history and global impact to life. Discover what it means to be Irish through exciting hands-on experiences for all ages. Then, as night falls, step into the magic of Wild Lights: Passport to Wonder at Dublin Zoo. Explore nine spectacular illuminated zones celebrating Ireland and cultures from around the world, with breathtaking lantern displays, colour and wonder around every corner.

Event Dates: 12th November 2026 – 5th January 2027 (Closed Christmas Eve, Christmas Day & St Stephen’s Day)

Wild Lights Hours: 5pm – 9pm on selected nights

events.title: The Dublin Double: EPIC Museum x Dublin Zoo Wild Lights
events.description:
By day, visitors can visit EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, Dublin’s award-winning interactive experience. The museum’s digital galleries, motion-sensor games and “passports” invite guests to explore what it truly means to be Irish – from music and sport to science, technology and literature.

By night, the adventure continues at Dublin Zoo’s Wild Lights, where the Zoo transforms into an illuminated world bursting with colour and larger-than-life installations.

From uncovering the remarkable journeys of Irish emigrants to strolling through enchanting trails of light, this new double offer brings together story, sparkle, and endless opportunities for unforgettable family photos – the perfect way to capture those precious memories.

events.title: Wild Lights at Dublin Zoo
events.description:
From November 12th, Ireland’s largest festival of lights returns to Dublin Zoo with a spectacular new experience, Passport to Wonder.

Step inside and discover nine immersive zones, where captivating celebrations and traditions from across the globe come alive through magnificent handcrafted lanterns, dazzling light, music, colour and movement.

Feel the beat of K-Pop. The enchantment of Ireland. The colour of Carnival. The glow of Diwali. And the magic of Christmas.

Nine zones. Countless moments of wonder. One unforgettable night.

This year, under 3s go free at Wild Lights. A little extra wonder for your family night out!

And every visit helps Dublin Zoo protect wildlife in Ireland and around the world.

events.title: Winter Cocktail Masterclass
events.description:
Step into the festive spirit with a Winter Cocktail Masterclass at the Irish Whiskey Museum, right in the heart of Dublin!

Begin your experience with a delicious, warming hot whiskey on arrival before stepping behind the bar for a fun, hands-on cocktail-making experience.

Guided by our expert mixologists, discover the art of crafting delicious winter-inspired cocktails, learn professional techniques and explore exciting flavours as you shake, stir and sip your own creations.

Whether you're celebrating with friends, planning a festive date or simply looking for something different to do in Dublin this winter, this interactive experience promises plenty of laughter, great drinks and unforgettable memories!

events.title: REWORKED: A Zero-Waste Jewellery Workshop with Shock of Grey
events.description:

Explore a collection of reclaimed beads, broken jewellery, chains, charms and other materials, then mix, match and reimagine them to create something completely your own.

Learn simple techniques for taking jewellery apart, combining unexpected materials and transforming unwanted pieces into something new and wearable. Bring along old or broken jewellery from home or choose from the materials provided.

Suitable for ages 12+, this relaxed workshop offers a playful introduction to creative reuse and zero-waste design. No experience is required and all tools and materials are supplied.

It’s the perfect blend of horror and holiday spirit—guaranteed to make your heart skip a beat and say “ho ho...noooo!

events.description:

These hands-on workshops encourage families to explore, imagine and make together while spending quality time in the museum. They also offer a wonderful opportunity to experience the museum's historic buildings and expansive grounds.

events.title: It's A Wonderful Life
events.description:
The play follows the life of George Bailey, a man with big dreams of travelling the world and building skyscrapers, who instead finds himself rooted in his hometown by duty and heart. On a fateful, snowy Christmas Eve, facing financial ruin and despair, George contemplates the unthinkable. It is then that he meets Clarissa Oddbody, an “Angel Second Class” who has been waiting over two hundred years to earn her wings.

It’s a Wonderful Life is a story of hope, redemption, and the reminder that every time a bell rings, an angel gets its wings.

21 Nov - 10 Jan 2027

“Never thinks about himself, God. That’s why he’s in trouble. He needs a Guardian Angel.”

events.title: Standing Ground: Ireland-France, Savoir-Faire, Innovation and the Future of Crafts
events.description:
A highlight of Design & Craft Council Ireland’s Irish Design Week 2026, Standing Ground: Ireland-France, Savoir-Faire, Innovation and the Future of Crafts celebrates the meeting of contemporary fashion and traditional craftsmanship. The exhibition showcases two haute couture gowns by Irish designer Michael Stewart, unveiled at Paris Haute Couture Week 2026.

The Carrickmacross Lace Dress required 4,300 hours of handwork by Monaghan artisans, while the Maison Vermont Dress reflects an award-winning collaboration between Stewart and the renowned French couture embroidery house. Together, the works demonstrate how centuries-old Irish and French craft traditions continue to inspire innovation in fashion today.

Free entry, no booking required.

events.description:
The exhibition examines how contemporary artists have responded to histories of political resistance, displacement, occupation, memory and solidarity through photography, sculpture, installation, film and painting.

Bringing together works by Tarek Al-Ghoussein, Basma Al Sharif, Simone Fattal, Shadi Habib Allah, Rula Halawani, Hazem Harb, Khalil Rabah and Abdul Hay Mosallam Zarara, the exhibition explores the diversity of Palestinian artistic practice across several generations.

events.title: The Seagull
events.description:
Irina, a fading star of the stage, returns to her family estate to see her volatile son Konstantin with her lover Boris in tow. Nina, an aspiring actress and Konstantin’s newest obsession, draws everyone into her orbit and the tensions simmering beneath the surface of this idyllic countryside retreat begin to bubble over. Ambitions collide, resentments surface and longing spirals out of control.

Following the successes of Uncle Vanya (2025) and A Streetcar Named Desire (2024), Cathal Cleary returns to Smock Alley this Christmas with another unmissable classic. The Seagull gets a bold, contemporary reimagining from Simon Stephens, bringing Chekhov’s famously dysfunctional family vividly into the here and now.

events.title: War of Independence Tour
events.description:
This specially researched tour will bring visitors through the events of the ‘Anglo-Irish War’. The tour will track the rise of Sinn Féin, the reorganisation of the Volunteers into the force known as the IRA, the development of guerilla warfare in Ireland, Britain’s political and military policy in Ireland, partition, and the consequences of the Treaty which ended it all.

Booking is essential, as availability is limited. The tour will last approximately one hour and fifteen minutes, and patrons are welcome to enjoy our exhibition at their own leisure after the tour.

This tour may not be suitable for children under the age of 12

events.title: NCH Landmarks: The Jimmy Cake - Brains
events.description:
The Jimmy Cake began life in Dublin in the late 1990s as das Madman, blazing briefly and chaotically, to burn out and reform at the turn of the century as a nine-piece band, blending accordion, clarinet, saxophone, glockenspiel, trumpet and DIY percussion around the core of guitars, bass and drums.

Brains was released on their own Pilatus label in 2001. In five tracks, they announced something hitherto unheard: at times raw, fearless and experimental, in other places fragile and intimate, moving restlessly between folk, post-rock grandeur and something far more elusive.

events.title: Christmas Tour of Dublin City by DoDublin Tours
events.description:
Get into the Christmas spirit with a magical open-top bus tour of Ireland’s capital! Every winter, Dublin City Council transforms the city into a wonderland with dazzling lights and imaginative displays. And what better way to soak it all in than from the top deck — an interactive and unforgettable way to experience Dublin at its festive best!

Gather your loved ones and step into the spirit of the season when joining Santa and his helpers for a heartwarming adventure through the sparkling streets of the capital. Route highlights include the Samuel Beckett Bridge, Grafton Street and more.

events.title: The Magic of Christmas at Airfield Estate
events.description:
Set amongst the natural beauty of Airfield, this reimagined experience is created with little ones in mind, blending timeless traditions with plenty of space to breathe.

After a busy year, our team of elves can’t wait to welcome you and yours to enjoy a fun-filled visit with Santa.

Visit on selected dates from November 28th to December 22nd 2026. See website for dates and times.

events.title: A Christmas to Remember
events.description:
Create cherished memories at A Christmas to Remember, a heartwarming festive journey through the historic setting of Newbridge House and Farm.

Begin with a cosy hot chocolate welcome before discovering reindeer food, Mrs Claus making Christmas puddings and an enchanting elves’ passageway leading through the farmyard and historic halls. Then, gather around the fireside for a personalised visit with Santa, before choosing a special gift in the Elves’ Toy Shop.

A nostalgic Christmas experience filled with warmth, wonder and magical moments the whole family will treasure.

events.title: Santa Paws
events.description:
Give Your Four-Legged Friend a Christmas to Remember!

This Christmas, bring the whole family — paws and all — to Santa Paws at Newbridge House & Farm!

Your furry friend can meet Santa, tell him their Christmas wishes and receive a special doggie gift to take home. You’ll also have the chance to capture a festive family photo with Santa using your own device, creating a precious memory to treasure.

With plenty of Christmas spirit and a beautiful historic setting, it’s the perfect festive outing for dog lovers and their four-legged companions.

Don’t let your dog be a grinch! Book your time slot and make Santa Paws part of your Christmas traditions this year.

events.title: Santa Experience at Croke Park
events.description:
During the Croke Park Santa Experience, visitors will peek inside the North Pole GAA Elf Dressing Rooms, before entering the Skills Zone, where they can play a ‘cool’ selection of fun, festive games. Then it will be time to step into Santa’s very special Croke Park cabin to meet the man himself. Every child will receive a small gift at the North Pole GAA Gifting Station, and photos will also be available to purchase.

Tickets include access to the GAA Museum where visitors can explore two floors of GAA exhibits. The experience lasts 50 minutes and is wheelchair and buggy accessible. Free parking is available outside the GAA Museum.

events.title: Santa at Malahide Castle
events.description:
Make this Christmas one to remember with a magical Santa experience in the enchanting surroundings of historic Malahide Castle.

Step into a world of festive wonder, soak up the Christmas atmosphere and meet Santa himself in a truly memorable setting. From sharing Christmas wishes to capturing those special moments together, this is an experience designed to make the season feel extra magical.

Perfect for families looking to create new traditions and treasured memories, Santa at Malahide Castle is a Christmas experience to enjoy together and remember for years to come.

Gather the family and make Santa’s visit part of your Christmas story this year!

events.title: In Conversation with Louise O'Neill on A Bigger Life
events.description:
Louise O’Neill is undoubtedly one of Ireland’s most acclaimed contemporary authors. Her complex, sharp novels, including Only Ever Yours, Asking for It and After the Silence, have earned her praise at home and internationally. A Bigger Life marks a departure from her previous work as her first full-length memoir.

As part of the book tour for A Bigger Life, which will be published by HarperCollins and available to purchase from 24th September 2026, Louise will join us at EPIC for an in-depth conversation about the memoir’s many themes and learnings, from women’s rage, to Y2K thinness, modern masculinity, romantic relationships and of course, emigration.

events.title: Fabric of a Nation | Fashion Tour
events.description:
This one-hour tour dives into the creative minds of Philip Treacy, Orla Kiely, Carmel Snow, Jonathan Anderson, and many more.

In celebration of the Dior Fall ‘27 Fashion Show, taking place in Trinity College on 4th December under Derry-man Jonathan Anderson’s creative direction, this tour explores fascinating stories from Irish diaspora design history, including:

- Wicklow woman Genevieve Figgis, the first Irish artist commissioned for Dior.

- The scandal of Olympic medallist Fanny Durack wearing a form-fitting swimsuit in 1912.

- Dalkey-born Carmel Snow, who became editor-in-chief of Harper’s Bazaar.

Perfect for those passionate about fashion, design and the Irish diaspora’s impact on the industry.

events.title: Rin
events.description:
A natural singer since childhood, Rin picked up the guitar during the pandemic, learning to play her favorite songs. That curiosity soon evolved into a desire to write her own.

Rin’s music radiates a kind of wide-eyed sincerity that’s both refreshing and nostalgic. Her debut project fawn, released in August 2025, marks the beginning of her coming-of-age story—an honest reflection of growth, heartbreak, and the pure emotion that comes from telling your story exactly as you feel it.

Plus support from Sara Baroni

Over 18s only.

events.title: Gareth
events.description:
Gareth’s covers has amassed tens of millions streams to date but it is his original music that has garnered critical acclaim. Just this past year, Gareth inked a publishing deal with BMG, a booking deal with UTA, and global distribution with Virgin Music Group. 2025 has been a year full of original music, featuring Gareth’s May EP release of “Steal Your Thunder.” That music has been featured on Absolute Country, Smooth Country, SiriusXM The Highway, and more.

events.title: FringePOP: AlanJames Burns—The Waking Walls
events.description:
First created over two days in September 2023, The Waking Walls was a caoineadh reverberating over the rippling waters of the Cavan lakelands, lamenting the ecological losses the Crannóg and its castle have witnessed over their lifetime.

Now reimagined as an immersive video installation, this collaborative artwork brings you back to the water, to the grief, to the bellowing keen of the crannóg.

The Waking Walls is a collaborative artwork by AlanJames Burns, with Chandrika Narayanan-Mohan, Anne Marie Hynes, Andrew Lynch, Trevor Whelan, Ben Glover, NYAH, Karina Lynch, Martin Donohoe, Jenny O’Hare, Laura O’Keeffe and Gearoid O’Hallmhurain.

events.title: Legends, Ghosts and Ghouls of Dublin | Walking Tour
events.description:
Kept alive in the histories of the Filí and the Seanchaidhe, Ireland’s gods were not destroyed but - in the words of Mark Williams - demoted to lesser beings. This is an important element of Ireland’s oral histories, which in turn have coloured its popular histories and left many legends for us to parse over today.

On the other side of Irish history we have the ballrooms, the salons, and the private studies of Dublin’s litterati. The seances and unwrapping parties, the mysteries and the macabre, all combining into the secret esoteric orders that strove to unlock the secrets of existence.

events.title: Street Art | Walking Tour
events.description:
our tour is the perfect place to get to know the local talent.

As far back as human beings have had walls to draw on, we’ve been doing it. From cave-painters to street-taggers, Graffiti has a universal attraction and a long love-hate story with city officials. Come delve into the details of Dublin’s graffiti scene and find out just how fuzzy the line can be between the legal murals and ‘illegal’ graffiti that color the Hibernian Metropolis.

events.title: Alternative Side to Dublin | FREE Walking Tour
events.description:
Ever wonder what’s down there? For such a small city, Dublin certainly has its fair share of secret spots and dodgy stories. Starting from the Garden of Remembrance, our guides will share the story of one of the Rising’s lesser known heroes, how Dublin’s aging buildings have been utilised (for better or worse), and some of the crazy nights of Dublin’s past. Whether new or old to the city, come find a few new spots to socialize and discover and Alternative Side of Dublin.

The Alternative Side of Dublin Tour is free to all and we are dedicated to keeping it that way, tipping if you can is greatly encouraged!

Our tour has over 100 excellent reviews online and is ranked in the top tours on Trip Advisor.

events.title: Wreath Decorating Workshop
events.description:
With cozy vibes, twinkly inspiration, and friendly guidance every step of the way, you’ll get to decorate your faux wreath with ribbons, ornaments and all the merry touches that will make your wreath unique. Bring your friends, your favorite beverage, and your holiday excitement then leave with a stunning wreath 🎄✨

WHAT EACH TICKET INCLUDES

Faux 45cm Christmas wreath

Ribbons, bows and other decorative pieces for your wreath

Chill vibes and good music!

THE RULES

This is over 18s. Our studio is a place for adults to socialize.

All attendees must have a valid ticket.

WHAT DO WE DO DURING THE WORKSHOP? DO WE HAVE TO FOLLOW ALONG?

events.title: Dublin True Crime | Walking Tour
events.description:
Murder, mystery and madness!

“Obedientia Civium, Urbis Felicitas” Have you ever wondered what the words under the Three Castles Burning mean? Dublin has a long and rich criminal culture that goes all the way back to the vikings who first gave the city its modern name. If you have a love of history and gallows’ humour, then this is the tour for you!

On our two-hour walk we will explore crimes from Georgian to Modern Dublin, giving context for how criminality influenced the city’s history, and was itself shaped by that history in turn. From Tiger Kidnappings to Heart Heists, come and hear the tale of Dublin’s dark deeds…

Aoife Grace Moore is editor at joe.ie, formerly a political correspondent for the BBC, and author of The Long Game.

Peter McGann is an Irish comedian, actor, writer and director, and a two-time Goss.ie Award nominee.

Jack Leavey of Basht. Basht is one of Ireland’s most exciting rock bands. Their new album, Poor Advice, is out now.

Your ticket includes a tour of the Teeling distillery and a whiskey tasting before the show.

events.title: NCH Landmarks : Mundy – Jelly Legs & 24 Star Hotel
events.description:
Mundy’s first album Jelly Legs was released in October 1996 to critical acclaim and went on to sell 50,000 copies. However it was his visceral debut single 'To You I Bestow' that garnered most attention after it was licensed to appear on the soundtrack to Baz Luhrmann’s adaptation of Shakespeare’s Romeo+ Juliet, this bestselling soundtrack went on to sell 11 million copies and introduced Mundy to the world.

Mundy released 24 Star Hotel in 2002 which went 3 x platinum, and his album Raining Down Arrows in 2004 went straight in to the Irish Charts at number 1.

Tickets €22, €30, €37.50

events.title: NSOI: Symphony Shorts Bernstein Symphonic Dances from West Side Story

Led by presenter and storyteller Jessie Grimes, the NCH Discover Artist-in-Residence, this fun and interactive concert is specially designed for children aged 6 and up.

With live music, playful storytelling, and amazing performances by NSOI, this relaxed and Autism Friendly concert is a fantastic way to experience music up close.

Adults €20, Child: €15, Family ticket (4, max 2 adults) €65

events.title: Krampus Night
events.description:
A Cure For Christmas

Aren’t Christmas puddings and mince pies terribly mediocre? Don’t carollers make you nauseous? Isn’t turkey an awfully dry bird? Have you ever stopped by a shopping centre in late December and felt nothing but gut-wrenching cynicism? When the nights draw in and the snow begins to fall, there’s only one good remedy for Christmas schmaltz and cheer.

Join us this December for a special, continental edition of Darkland - and leave the ribbons and sleighbells at home. Devised with the Scrooges and Grinches in mind; indulge in grim and spooky stories from our expert storytellers. Krampus is going to have a busy night at the museum - for we have been very naughty indeed.

events.title: The CHQ Tour | One of Dublin’s Iconic Buildings
events.description:
This is a rare opportunity to explore the rich heritage of the Docklands area and uncover the unique story behind the building, its architecture, and its role in shaping the city. The CHQ Building, originally known as Stack A, was constructed in the early 19th century as part of the broader Custom House docks complex. This tour offers the chance to step back in time and discover the building’s original purpose as a bonded warehouse for storing valuable cargo including tobacco, tea, wine and spirits.

On the CHQ tour, you’ll also hear the fascinating story of its transformation into a grand Banqueting Hall in 1856, when thousands gathered for an enormous celebration in honour of Irish soldiers returning from the Crimean War.

The tour ends in the most unusual of Christmas venues—a former historic church, now an iconic cafe/bar—where you can enjoy a festive drink (two for one, our Christmas gift to you). With Dublin's northerly latitude, darkness falls from 3:30pm in December, and that's when the city's magic truly begins.

events.title: Joyce DiDonato Vocal Masterclass
events.description:
Open to singers and vocal students, this unique opportunity offers participants the chance to work directly with one of the world's most celebrated artists, gaining invaluable insights into vocal technique, interpretation, performance, and artistic development.

Multi-Grammy Award winner and 2018 Olivier Award winner for Outstanding Achievement in Opera, Kansas-born Joyce DiDonato entrances audiences across the globe, and has been proclaimed “perhaps the most potent female singer of her generation” by The New Yorker.

events.title: Éire to Everywhere: Stories Without Borders with Dr. Don Gillis on Ray Flynn and the Irish Diaspora
events.description:
Author Dr. Don Gillis discusses his book, The Battle for Boston: Race, Class, and the Future of Progressive Cities, exploring the life and legacy of former Boston Mayor Ray Flynn, his advocacy for racial justice, support for the MacBride Principles, and efforts to strengthen ties between Ireland and the United States.

Boston Mayor Ray Flynn, one of the most influential Irish-American political leaders of the late twentieth century examines how Flynn's Irish identity informed his leadership in Boston, his advocacy for racial justice, his support for the MacBride Principles in Northern Ireland, and his efforts to strengthen economic and cultural ties between Ireland and Boston through Boston Ireland Ventures.

In 2024, ahead of Taylor’s sold-out Eras Tour, the Irish Family History Centre did some digging into the popstar’s genealogy. Turned out there was more to the singer’s love of Aran jumpers and the Irish druid aesthetic for her 2020 album Folklore than just preference – there’s Irish in her blood.

As a result of the research, a specialised themed tour for Swifties was created; the EPIC Museum, seen through a fresh lens, by uncovering the roots of one Miss Taylor Alison Swift, and her many connections to Ireland, whether it’s the inspiration behind one of her albums, her fashion sense, or her lyricism.

The Irish Family History Centre is available to assist visitors in their genealogy journey, based on-site at EPIC.

events.title: Romantic Dublin with a nod to St Valentine!
events.description: Even through centuries of war, hardship and poverty, Dublin has always found room for love stories that capture the public imagination. Irish mythology, too, is rich with tales of heroic romance between warriors and captivating princesses. This tour winds through the city's hidden corners, uncovering these stories—many with surprisingly tragic endings! We'll also explore Dublin's unexpected connection to St Valentine himself: his mortal remains rest not in Rome, but in a casket within a Dublin church! The tour concludes in a former church, once the site of a notable wedding or two, where you'll enjoy two romantic drinks for the price of one.

events.title: Frederick Douglass & His Irish Connections
events.description:
Frederick Douglass (1818–1895) was a renowned African American abolitionist, orator, publisher and author—reportedly the most photographed American of the 19th century.

Recently escaped from slavery, Douglass arrived in Dublin in 1845, staying four months to publish his first autobiography, deliver lectures, and meet activists like Daniel O'Connell. He later made four visits to Belfast in 1846. We'll explore Dublin sites tied to his time here, set against political change: relief for Irish Catholics, yet widespread poverty and a famine gripping the countryside. Douglass was deeply moved by Ireland's underclass and those working to relieve it.

From world premieres to intimate screenings, exclusive Q&As to parties and celebrations, DIFF offers a unique journey into the world of film, all set against the backdrop of buzz of the Irish capital.

We welcome the lovers, the dreamers, and the curious newcomers.

Join us and be part of a contemporary cinema experience that connects communities, ignites ideas, and inspires a love for cinema that lasts all year round.

events.title: Mary Coughlan
events.description:
Born in Shantalla, Galway city, Mary has made some of the most uncompromising, wholly personal, and universal music by any Irish artist. While her roots are in jazz and blues – Billie Holiday and Bessie Smith are among her inspirations – pop, rock, folk, and chanson (Edith Piaf is also a touchstone) influences also appear in her work. Now, the next chapter of her distinguished career finds her exploring a little known side of the music of Peggy Lee.

Never one to sit still, Mary is now planning her most ambitious project to date. While she has covered Billie Holiday, Joy Division, and The Blue Nile in the past, she intends to reimagine the album Peggy Lee made with the pioneering rock’n’roll songwriters Lieber and Stoller.
